records.text: Bradley D. Hansell was one of the VIPs aboard SAM 702 when it left Fort Huachuca for El Paso on the morning of September 9, apparently traveling with four other people.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: SAM 702 was leaving Fort Huachuca and heading for El Paso, Texas, in a time frame that would work with this alleged meeting on the morning of September 9th. ... And now we can reveal the name of one of those VIPs who was aboard the plane, apparently with four other people. ... His name is Bradley Hansell.

verification.notes: Bradley Hansell’s official biography confirms his identity and role, but no authoritative passenger manifest or flight log located establishes that he and four other people were aboard SAM702 on the claimed trip. Audited private-travel-record limitation; verification was attempted.

records.text: Candace Owens said the plane flew from Fort Huachuca to El Paso on September 9, arrived at 1:20 p.m. local time, remained for four hours and ten minutes, and returned to Joint Base Andrews.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: then flies from Fort Huachuca to El Paso and arrives at 1 20 p.m local remains on the ground for four hours and 10 minutes and then it returns back to Joint Base Andrews just outside of DC

verification.notes: Current searches found no authoritative aircraft log or official itinerary confirming the claimed September 9 Fort Huachuca-El Paso-Joint Base Andrews route, 1:20 p.m. arrival, or four-hour-ten-minute ground time. The episode’s assertion alone is insufficient.

records.text: The Office of the Secretary of Defense said it could not respond to the FOIA request within the statutory 20-day period because unusual circumstances affected its ability to process the request quickly.
records.speaker: Office of the Secretary of Defense

appearances.snippet: Although we have already begun processing your request, we will not be able to respond within the FOIA's 20-day statutory time period as there are unusual circumstances which impact our ability to quickly process your request.

verification.notes: The primary episode reads the Office of the Secretary of Defense response stating that processing had begun but a response could not be made within FOIA’s 20-day period because unusual circumstances affected prompt processing. The statutory FOIA text independently confirms the 20-day determination period and written-notice extension for unusual circumstances.

records.text: Candace Owens said she had confirmed that Bradley Hansell's flight was booked from his office.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: He works for the Department of War and it was the flight was booked from his office. I've confirmed that.

verification.notes: The transcript records Owens saying she had confirmed the booking source, but current research found no booking record, travel-order document, named confirming source, or official response showing that Hansell’s office booked the flight.

records.text: Owens said SAM 702 flew to Tucson on September 8, two days before Charlie Kirk's assassination, remained there about four hours, stayed overnight at Fort Huachuca, and departed for El Paso the next morning.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: The plane that flew to Tucson, Arizona on September 8th, two days before Charlie (Charlie Kirk)'s assassination, landed and hung out in Tucson for about four hours before it carried on to the intel base in Fort Huachuca, Arizona, where it stayed overnight. ... Now, before departing for El Paso, Texas, the next morning—mid-morning on the 9th—it leaves for Texas.

verification.notes: Searches for the SAM 702 identifier and the claimed Tucson, Fort Huachuca, and El Paso itinerary produced no authoritative flight record or official confirmation. Public repetitions trace back to the same podcast investigation.

records.text: Owens said the office of Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence Bradley Hansell organized SAM 702.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Now, the person whose office organized that plane is the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, a man named Bradley Hansell.

verification.notes: Official sources confirm Bradley Hansell held the intelligence and security post, but no public manifest, tasking order, or official record verifies that his office organized the flight called SAM 702.

records.text: Owens reported that Mitch Snow believed he saw Brian Harpole at a meeting near Fort Huachuca on the morning associated with SAM 702.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That plane has been a source of interest due to a meeting which Mitch Snow stumbled upon that morning accidentally. ... And the meeting in which Mitch Snow believes that he saw Brian Harpole. Okay. Maybe, maybe he didn't. I was always open to that.

verification.notes: The statement is limited to reporting the stated belief of Mitch Snow, not proving that Brian Harpole was present. A published transcript of the Snow interview confirms that Snow made the identification with explicit uncertainty; independent evidence does not establish the underlying sighting.

sources.title: Candace Owens Interviews Military Eyewitness Mitch Snow
sources.relevance: Publishes the source interview and preserves the uncertainty attached to the Harpole identification.
